transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21 09:42 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Morales (Redwood), Priya Shah (Harbor CTO), Marco Ruiz (Harbor Lead ML), Elena Park (Product), Tom Bennett (Infra)

Summary: Quick Optimize-led walkthrough covering batching, prefix/KV caching, and streaming vs batch tradeoffs. Ran live cost-sim with rough numbers for Harbor Tech's conversational search workload. Agreed on next steps: Redwood to send detailed cost simulation workbook and recorded console demo; Harbor to provide anonymized traffic traces for pilot sizing.

Topics: cost-simulation overview; prefix cache strategies; KV prefetch heuristics; continuous batching and streaming tradeoffs; dedicated vs hosted routing for throughput; pilot scope and timelines.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay everyone, welcome. Uh this is Maya from Redwood, thanks for making time, we'll keep this tight. We have Liam and Sofia with me. Priya, Marco, you there?
[00:08] Priya Shah: Yep, here. Thanks, Maya.
[00:10] Marco Ruiz: Morning. Tom and I are on..
[00:12] Tom Bennett: hi, sorry bit of background noise.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: No worries. Quick agenda: we'll walk through Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix/KV cache, run a couple of cost sim scenarios in the console, and map pilot next steps.
[00:25] Elena Park: Sounds good. Our key success criteria: reduce per-request cost by at least 40% without exceeding 120ms p95 latency for search responses.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Great, we'll aim the sim at that. Marco, can you remind us of current qps and avg tokens?
[00:38] Marco Ruiz: Sure. Baseline is about 85 RPS sustained during peak, average prompt+response token count around 320 tokens, but there's a long tail - some sessions go to 1.2k tokens. Most traffic is conversational search with short prompts followed by longer context.
[00:53] Liam O'Connor: That tail is important for prefetch. For prefix cache we usually see big wins when you have repeated session prefixes - like rerank or search context. Do you have session affinity?
[01:02] Marco Ruiz: Yes we stick sessions to a shard for 30 minutes, but replays happen across devices.
[01:07] Liam O'Connor: Good. Okay, quick high level: two levers - continuous batching (improve GPU utilization) and prefix/KV caching (reduce decoded tokens + compute). We'll demo a conservative vs aggressive prefetch policy in the console.
[01:20] [00:01:20] (crosstalk)
[01:22] Priya Shah: Quick question — are you expecting we need dedicated GPUs or can hosted run this? Cost is a factor.
[01:27] Maya Chen: We can run both. Hosted is fastest to onboard; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better unit-cost at high sustained RPS. For 85 RPS sustained, you might be borderline — depends on batch sizes and concurrency. We'll show numbers.
[01:39] Liam O'Connor: Opening the Optimize console now — apologies if cursor jumps, network's a bit choppy.
[01:45] [00:01:45] Liam: Okay, pulling up Harbor Tech sample profile — note: this is synthetic based on your earlier notes; we'll update with your logs later.
[01:53] Liam: First scenario, conservative prefetch: we prefetch KV for top-3 prefixes when session token length > 50 and only for requests from known users. This adds about a 15ms hit on the edge but reduces model decode by roughly 28% in our sim.
[02:08] Elena Park: So that 28% is on decode cost only? What about total latency?
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: Total p95 went from 150ms to 118ms in the sim because reduced model time outweighed the extra cache fetch time. But simulation caveat — network to KV store matters.
[02:23] Marco Ruiz: What KV backend are you assuming? Our infra uses managed Redis in us-west-2.
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: We're modeling a 2-3ms local Redis RTT. If yours is cross-AZ and higher, we can parametrically adjust.
[02:35] Maya Chen: Let's flip to aggressive prefetch for a minute.
[02:38] [00:02:38] Liam: Aggressive policy: prefetch top-10 prefixes + speculative KV priming when session length crosses 80 tokens. This yields up to 55% decode savings in the sim but increases precache bandwidth and cache write ops.
[02:52] Tom Bennett: Interesting — what's the cost tradeoff? More Redis operations cost more in infra and may require bigger cache nodes.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: Right. The cost-sim shows net savings if model token cost per decode >> KV op cost. For example, in our sim using a 32-bit float model at $0.00012 per token equivalent, the aggressive prefetch saved about 38% overall unit cost despite a 12% increase in cache infra.
[03:16] Priya Shah: Wait, you're using 32-bit model numbers — are you modeling quantized variants? We run - we prefer 4-bit quant on some workloads.
[03:23] Sofia Morales: Good catch. The sim has lines for fp16, int8 and q4. For Harbor's workload fp16 and q4 compare differently: q4 reduces model compute cost by ~45% but slightly increases latency jitter. We can lock to your preferred model family.
[03:37] Marco Ruiz: For production we want Q4 on most traffic but keep fp16 for long context or hallucination-sensitive flows.
[03:44] Liam O'Connor: Totally reasonable. In the console I've switched sim to q4b; let me re-run the scenario — gives slightly different ratios: aggressive prefetch still saves ~30% unit cost overall because KV ops are cheap relative to token decode even under q4.
[03:58] [00:03:58] (typing sounds)
[04:02] Maya Chen: Another lever is batching. We saw you have peaks at 140 RPS during spikes — are those spikes short?
[04:09] Marco Ruiz: Usually 3-7 minutes, triggered by marketing events.
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: Continuous batching we recommend combined with adaptive concurrency. If you allow micro-batching up to 20ms latency slack, you can increase batch size and reduce token compute per-request. The cost-sim has a slider for batching window; moving from 1ms to 20ms increased average batch size from 3 to 12 and saved ~22% in model cost without breaching 120ms p95 in our sim.
[04:34] Elena Park: But our UX team worries about adding tail latency. How do we set SLOs?
[04:39] Maya Chen: You can define per-route latency budgets in Console and Optimize will propose batching targets that respect p99 or p95 budgets. Also we can set gradual rollout: start with 5% traffic for increased batching then ramp.
[04:50] Priya Shah: Are rollbacks automatic?
[04:52] Liam O'Connor: Yes, you can configure automatic fallback to smaller batch sizes or different model variant if latency crosses thresholds. It’s in the rollout policy section — we'll show that.
[05:00] [00:05:00] Liam: Switching to the rollout tab — here's an example canary: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> full over 48 hours with automatic rollback at 130ms p99.
[05:13] Marco Ruiz: Can you show the per-token cost breakdown? I want to see edge, model, and cache ops separated.
[05:18] Liam O'Connor: Sure. Console shows token-level: model compute 72%, KV ops 8%, network/edge 10%, other overhead 10% in conservative case. In aggressive case model compute drops to 45% and KV ops rise to 20% — net unit cost drops.
[05:33] Maya Chen: We're linking to a short notes doc in chat — the cost-sim workbook also has a CSV you can download.
[05:40] [00:05:40] (chat message: https://redwood.app/sim/harbor-ht-sim-1216 )
[05:45] Priya Shah: I clicked, getting a 403 - looks like not-public.
[05:47] Maya Chen: Sorry, I'll adjust permissions after the call and attach in follow up.
[05:51] Tom Bennett: Security question — for KV prefetch we assume token-level cache keys may contain PII. How is that handled?
[05:58] Sofia Morales: Great question. For Private/Dedicated we can configure KMS-wrapped encryption for KV entries and redact PII with pre-cache hooks. You can also choose TTLs and access controls per route.
[06:10] Marco Ruiz: Do you have SOC2 docs / PEN test reports?
[06:13] Maya Chen: Yes, we will attach SOC2 Type II and the pen test summary in the follow-up email.
[06:18] Priya Shah: Good. Also curious about cross-region fallback — if prefetch fails or KV misses in us-west, can requests route to hosted fallback without losing SLA?
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: Yes, that's part of Smart Routing. You can set fallback model variants or regions. If KV miss rates increase, we can fall back to a lower-latency variant or increase batching to amortize cost.
[06:38] [00:06:38] (brief pause)
[06:41] Liam O'Connor: Okay, running an end-to-end sim: 85 RPS baseline, q4 model, 320 avg tokens, peak 140 RPS. Conservative prefetch + batching window 10ms -> projected 39% cost reduction, p95 112ms. Aggressive prefetch + batching 20ms -> projected 52% cost reduction, p95 125ms (slightly over your target).
[07:10] Elena Park: So aggressive meets cost but may break latency SLO. Can we tune hybrid: aggressive prefetch for low-length sessions and conservative for long sessions?
[07:18] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. Optimize supports per-route and per-session rules — e.g., session length > 800 tokens keep conservative decode path; short sessions go aggressive. That often gets you best of both.
[07:29] Marco Ruiz: What about cache consistency when we push new model versions? Prefetched KVs could become stale.
[07:36] Sofia Morales: We recommend namespacing keys by model version and using a short TTL during rollout. Also console has a model-aware invalidation API you can call during rollout.
[07:46] Priya Shah: Nice. One more — billing visibility. Can we get token-level and route-level breakdowns for chargeback?
[07:53] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token and cost breakdown with exportable CSV and an API for programmatic ingestion to your billing system.
[08:02] [00:08:02] (typing)
[08:05] Marco Ruiz: For the pilot, what would you recommend we start with?
[08:08] Liam O'Connor: Start with a small subset of traffic: e.g., 10% of traffic on search route with hybrid prefetch (aggressive for short sessions) and batching window 12ms. Run for 2 weeks and measure p95/p99 and cost delta. We'll instrument with tracing hooks so you can see where tokens saved.
[08:23] Maya Chen: We're going to attach a recommended pilot config and a short checklist in follow-up.
[08:28] Priya Shah: Timeline wise we want data before fiscal planning in first week of Jan. Can you get us the sim and recordings by Jan 4?
[08:34] Maya Chen: Yes — action item for me.
[08:36] [00:08:36] (brief background noise)
[08:39] Tom Bennett: From infra: any special network requirements for private? We need IP allowlists or peering set up?
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: For Private deployment yes we'll need VPC peering and NAT config; for dedicated hosted we can do TLS-over-public endpoints with client certs. We'll send infra checklist.
[08:55] Marco Ruiz: Can you simulate a marketing spike — 4x traffic for 6 minutes — and show whether autoscale / batching holds p95?
[09:03] Liam O'Connor: Yup, run that now — (typing) — with the hybrid policy autoscale to Reserved burst capacity and batching window 20ms, simulated p95 stays at ~140ms, p99 at 220ms. Without dedicated reserved capacity p99 jumps to 520ms and many requests get queued.
[09:21] Priya Shah: Ok that's useful — we may need a small reserved burst pool for events.
[09:26] Maya Chen: Good note. We'll add recommended sizing for events in the workbook.
[09:30] [00:09:30] Liam O'Connor: Sharing a short deck link in chat that summarizes the recs and cost-breakdowns.
[09:35] [chat link: https://redwood.app/decks/harbor-optimize-summary.pdf ]
[09:38] Elena Park: Great. Quick nit — in the sim it looked like prefix cache keys included user IDs. We'll need to make sure we hash or tokenize keys to avoid leaking PII.
[09:46] Sofia Morales: Absolutely — our best practices include key hashing and partial redaction. We'll include an example transform rule.
[09:52] Marco Ruiz: Anything else on compliance? We need to see SOC2 and FedRAMP roadmap for some enterprise customers.
[09:57] Maya Chen: We'll include SOC2 docs; FedRAMP is on our roadmap and we can share an ETA and controls mapping currently.
[10:04] [00:10:04] (closing notes)
[10:06] Maya Chen: All right, to recap: Redwood will send the cost-sim workbook, console recording, SOC2 docs and infra checklist by Jan 4. Harbor will send anonymized 7-day request logs and confirm pilot traffic slice. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for week of Jan 10. Action items captured in chat.
[10:20] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone. Marco and Tom will coordinate logs.
[10:23] Marco Ruiz: Yep, will do.
[10:25] Maya Chen: Thanks all. Bye.

Questions noted during call:
- What KV backend latency is assumed? (Answered: 2-3ms in sim, parametric)
- How are keys protected with PII? (Answered: key hashing, redaction, KMS wrap for Private)
- Can rollouts auto-rollback? (Answered: yes, configurable)

References/shared artifacts:
- Cost sim (console link) - https://redwood.app/sim/harbor-ht-sim-1216 (permission will be updated)
